target.title: fix: pace delivery recovery after startup outages
target.body:
Closes #101058

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where startup delivery recovery could replay many already-eligible queued messages in a tight burst after an outage or restart. That burst can concentrate outbound sends against channel/provider rate limits even though each individual delivery is retried sequentially.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup recovery now applies a small shared pacing delay between actual replay attempts for outbound deliveries and session deliveries. Backoff skips, max-retry moves, reconnect drains, and first-entry recovery semantics stay unchanged. The pacing sleep is excluded from the active recovery budget, so a large already-eligible backlog is not deferred solely because recovery is sleeping between sends; genuinely exhausted recovery work still defers cleanly.

## User Impact

Queued messages recovered after a restart are replayed more gently instead of all eligible entries being sent back-to-back. This should reduce avoidable 429s and temporary outbound delivery failures after longer outages while preserving existing retry and reconnect behavior.

## Evidence

Before premise, source at base `60ce506712295e03d53cd4b91f4472f61d5971a6`: `recoverPendingDeliveries` sorted pending entries and immediately iterated them with `for (const entry of pending)` before calling `drainQueuedEntry`; `recoverPendingSessionDeliveries` had the same tight startup loop. There was no sleep, pacing helper, or jitter between eligible replays.

After behavior proof, real SQLite queue recovery via `node --import tsx --input-type=module` against this branch:

```json
{
  "spacingMs": 250,
  "summary": {
    "recovered": 2,
    "failed": 0,
    "skippedMaxRetries": 0,
    "deferredBackoff": 0
  },
  "deliveryTimes": [
    { "to": "target-a" },
    { "to": "target-b" }
  ],
  "deltaMs": 252,
  "recoveredLogCount": 2
}
```

Review follow-up: ClawSweeper flagged that counting the 250ms pacing sleep against the 60s startup budget could strand eligible backlog tails. The follow-up commit tracks pacing sleep separately from active recovery time and adds outbound + session regression tests using `maxRecoveryMs: 1` with three eligible entries; both paths still recover all three entries at 250ms intervals instead of deferring the tail.
